messages.subject: Question on MVC in Shiny
parts:
Hi, having no other clue I try here. Assume two input(s), a textfield called stock and a selection called popular. I'd like to have a reactive which can see both and if the input come from the text field then name will be loaded with the text, if the input comes from the selection then name will be loaded with the selected. In principle I need two controls than can write on the same model.


  getStockName<-reactive({
    print ("get name ...")

   name <-   ...some code here ...   
   
    print (name)
    return (name)
  })


Thanks in advance

messages.author: 0aa9f8b0b6c58de0
messages.subject: Re: Question on MVC in Shiny
parts:
Well, I answer myself just in case anyone has a similar issue, I solved placing in server the following ...

  observe({
    popular <- input$popular
    updateTextInput(session,"stock",value = popular)
  })

which forces the text input to take the value of the selection and then trigger the event to the rest of reactive.

Though I am not sure this is the most elegant way to do.

messages.subject: Re: Question on MVC in Shiny
parts:
Unless you do something like the solution you came up with, I'm not sure how the UI would make sense. If you type text in the textbox and then make a selection in the select box, then the textbox is ignored? Until you make another entry in the textbox, and then the select box is ignored? It seems like it will be confusing for the user.

Are you aware that the select input can also let you create new items? See select #3 on this app: http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/selectize-examples.html (source code is available at the link at the top)
